title: introduce-conflation-runner-with-fidelity-checksum-exporter
author: Emily Chen
description:
Motivation: Some production workloads present correlated short-turn conversations that together exercise a model's KV-cache and batching behavior in ways single-session runners don't capture. This PR adds a lightweight 'conflation' workload runner that stitches many short sequences into compound sessions with configurable correlation patterns and a compact fidelity checksum exporter to detect subtle output regressions over long-phase runs.

What this changes: Adds a new runner (benchmark_lab/conflation_runner.py) that generates multi-segment sessions using template-driven primers, inter-segment randomness controls, and target inter-arrival distributions. A reporting pipeline component (benchmark_lab/reporters/fidelity_checksum_exporter.py) consumes tokenized outputs and emits epoch-level checksums and summary artifacts (CSV + gzipped checksums) designed to be small enough for long baseline retention. The exporter also records deterministic sampling seeds for replay.

Why it's different: Existing runners focus on single-session fidelity or heavy multimodel mixes. The conflation runner targets the intermediate regime — many short prompts concatenated into a single logical session to trigger KV-cache churn and nontrivial batching composition effects. The fidelity checksum is intentionally lossy (rolling 64-bit xor + salted Murmur3) to be both compact and sensitive to order and small token deltas while avoiding storing full transcripts.

Compatibility and safety: No model weights are included. The runner and exporter are purely benchmarking tooling and run under existing benchmark lab configs. Default runs are non-destructive; seeds are logged for deterministic replays.

Testing and validation: Added unit tests for the checksum algorithm and deterministic replay harness (tests/test_conflation_runner.py, tests/test_fidelity_exporter.py). Included an integration SLO run script (scripts/integration_conflation.sh) used to produce the numbers in the PR description. Performance baseline: on a 4-A100 mini-cluster with 8 concurrent conflated sessions (avg 120 tokens/session) we see a 12-18% increase in KV eviction events and a 7-10% p95 latency delta compared to an equivalent non-conflated mix; these deltas are exactly the kind of signal downstream routing/quantization tools need to optimize.

Migration notes: Users of the benchmark harness can enable the runner by adding "conflation" to benchmark_config.workload_types; exporter writes to existing report buckets by default. Release notes below.

Related work: ENG-2193 (fidelity tooling roadmap), ENG-2367 (kv-cache churn investigations).

How to review: Start with benchmark_lab/conflation_runner.py for the core synthesis logic and benchmark_lab/reporters/fidelity_checksum_exporter.py for the compact artifact schema. Tests and integration script are in the tests/ and scripts/ directories respectively.

Changelog: New feature: conflation workload + fidelity checksum exporter. No breaking API changes.
